entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Yoshizawa-san, you drink hot beverages[n]even in the summer?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I have to prevent my body from getting[n]too cold, since the meet's coming up[n]rather soon.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I see, you make sure you're covering[n]all your bases.
Your drink's just as hot.
So what do you have, Akechi?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Good point.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Well, some people say coffee can cool[n]you off, even when hot, so I try to avoid[n]that too.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I had this image that you enjoy sweet[n]things, Akechi-san—is that untrue?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I swear I saw you eating fried sweet[n]bread on TV just the other day...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: It's all part of a marketing strategy. That[n]sort of stunt is an easy crowd-pleaser.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: You seem to have your own bases[n]covered as well.
I feel lied to...
I wish I hadn't learned that...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Presenting oneself in a favorable light[n]is nothing surprising.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: More surprising is just how innocent[n]you seem to be.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Haha, you're more innocent than I had[n]expected.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I've been wondering: how do you two[n]know each other?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: His social studies class visited the set[n]of a TV show I appeared on.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Ah, that's right. Second-years got to[n]go to a TV station.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: He and I exchanged our opinions[n]during the shoot and his way of[n]thinking intrigued me.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I can definitely see that![n][lName]-senpai's take on[n]things often helps me as well.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: That reminds me, Yoshizawa-san.[n]You had mentioned that he's been[n]providing you with some guidance.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Yes—like you just said, his way of[n]thinking is intriguing. I figured[n]I could benefit from his input.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: In that case, let's play a little game...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Would you mind if I posed the same[n]question to you that I first asked him?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: No, go right ahead.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: So, my question was...

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: What do you think of the Phantom[n]Thieves, Yoshizawa-san?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: The Phantom Thieves?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: You mean in the case that they do[n]in fact exist, yes?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I admit that the assistance of others[n]in need is a truly great act...

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: But I simply can't agree with their[n]methods.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I see. Care to explain why?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I suspect the Phantom Thieves' existence[n]isn't going to be beneficial to society in[n]the long run.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: How so?

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Well, for example, when someone's faced[n]with a problem to overcome, I believe[n]they need to do it themselves.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Getting help from others is totally fine,[n]but in the end, it takes a person's[n]initiative to truly create lasting change.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: If society relied upon a safety net like the[n]Phantom Thieves, I worry that people[n]would stop making a conscious effort.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Granted, this depends on how severe the[n]problem is, and it's inaccurate to apply[n]generalizations to an entire population...

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: But I believe a society where everyone[n]simply leaves matters to the Phantom[n]Thieves wouldn't last for very long.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I see... So, in the sense of a person's[n]growth, their actions actually hinder it.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Quite an interesting take on the matter.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Let me ask you, then—what do you[n]think of Yoshizawa-san's opinion?
She's not wrong.
It's a unique stance.
That was helpful.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Ah, so you think you should let others[n]come to their own conclusions on[n]the matter.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Haha, quite. I'd say it's equally as[n]unique as your own opinions.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I have to agree. It was quite inspiring[n]for myself as well.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Wait... Could you actually be a fan of the[n]Phantom Thieves, [lName]-senpai!?

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: I didn't mean to start an argument.[n]I just can't help myself sometimes.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Let's change the subject to something[n]a bit lighter.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: I'm sorry, I should probably get going...

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: If I'm away from home too late,[n]my parents will begin to worry.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Right, then let's call it a day.

entries.speaker: Akechi
entries.en: Good luck on your competition.
I'll be rooting for you.
You got this.

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Yes! Thank you!

entries.speaker: Kasumi
entries.en: Well then, see you later!
